extracted.intended_audience: Entities, applicants, and counsel participating in FCC spectrum auctions (short-form and long-form applicants), and auction compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for filing short-form and long-form applications, certifications, payments, communications prohibitions, and designated-entity eligibility in FCC spectrum auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of no default or delinquency
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that the applicant is not in default on any Commission licenses and is not delinquent on any non-tax debt owed to any Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may exclude a former default or delinquency if it has been resolved and meets any of: (A) notice received more than seven years before the short-form deadline; (B) default/delinquency amounted to less than $100,000; (C) paid within two quarters (6 months) after notice of final payment deadline; or (D) default/delinquency was subject to legal/arbitration proceeding that was cured upon resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: National-security-related bidder disqualification certification
rubrics_metrics.description: For auctions required under Title VI of Pub. L. 112-96 or involving spectrum made available under 47 U.S.C. 309(j)(8)(G)(i), applicants must certify under penalty of perjury that the applicant and disclosed persons are not barred for national-security reasons from bidding, participating, or receiving grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'person' includes individuals, partnerships, associations, joint-stock companies, trusts, or corporations; 'reasons of national security' means matters relating to national defense and foreign relations of the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on filing short-form applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual or entity may file more than one short-form application or have a controlling interest in more than one short-form application in any auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a consortium, each member is treated as having a controlling interest. Overlapping controlling interests cause both applications to be deemed incomplete, and only one applicant may be deemed qualified. Exception: qualifying rural wireless partnerships (per specific settlement criteria) and their individual members (≤25% ownership and other certification requirements) are exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'controlling interest' (de jure and de facto)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling interest includes individuals or entities with positive or negative de jure or de facto control of the applicant. De jure control includes holding 50 percent or more of voting stock or holding a general partnership interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership held indirectly through intervening corporations may be determined by successive multiplication of percentages; if any link meets/exceeds 50% or represents actual control it may be treated as 100%. De facto control is case-by-case; examples: constituting/appointing 50%+ of board, authority to appoint/promote/fire senior executives, or playing an integral role in management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'consortium'
rubrics_metrics.description: A consortium means an entity formed to apply as a single applicant to bid at auction pursuant to an agreement by two or more separate and distinct legal entities that individually are eligible to claim the same designated entity benefits under § 1.2110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No member of the consortium may be a nationwide provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'joint venture'
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint venture means a legally cognizable entity formed to apply as a single applicant to bid at auction pursuant to an agreement by two or more separate and distinct legal entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No member of the joint venture may be a nationwide provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'solely operational agreement'
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement, arrangement, or understanding addressing operational aspects of providing mobile service (e.g., roaming, device acquisition, spectrum leasing) provided it does not both relate to the licenses at auction and address or communicate, directly or indirectly, bidding at auction or bidding strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agreement both relates to the licenses at auction and addresses bidding/pricing/strategies (including specific licenses to bid or not), it is not a 'solely operational agreement.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may request additional informational submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may request applicants to submit additional information for informational purposes to aid in preparation of reports to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form applications missing required certifications are unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any short-form application (FCC Form 175) that does not contain all required certifications is unacceptable for filing and cannot be corrected after the filing deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an application will be deemed incomplete, the applicant will not be qualified to bid, and any upfront payment, if paid, will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications / common control rule for completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual/entity submits multiple applications in a single auction or commonly controlled entities submit applications for overlapping areas, only one may be deemed complete; others are incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with incomplete applications will not be qualified to bid and associated upfront payments will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to cure defects and amendment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will provide a limited opportunity to cure identified defects (except failure to sign or make required certifications) and to resubmit corrected short-form applications during a resubmission period; after that, only minor amendments are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major amendments cannot be made after the initial filing deadline; major amendments include ownership changes constituting assignment or transfer of control, changes in applicant size affecting designated-entity eligibility, and changes in license service areas intended to bid. Minor amendments include typographical corrections and other minor defects. An application amended by a major amendment is considered newly filed and may not be resubmitted after deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely correct defects results in dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who fail to correct defects in a timely manner as specified by public notice will have their applications dismissed with no opportunity to resubmit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing obligation to update pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must promptly amend or modify pending applications to maintain accuracy and completeness of furnished information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be made as promptly as possible, and in no case more than five business days after applicants become aware of the need to amend or five business days after the reportable event occurs, whichever is later. Obligation continues until amendments are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain communications after short-form filing
rubrics_metrics.description: After the short-form application filing deadline, applicants are prohibited until after the down payment deadline from cooperating, collaborating, communicating, or disclosing to each other or to non-applicant nationwide providers the substance of their own or others' bids or bidding strategies (including post-auction market structure), or from discussing/negotiating settlement agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications within the scope of agreements described in paragraphs (a)(2)(ix)(A)-(C) that are properly disclosed pursuant to paragraph (a)(2)(viii) are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls requirement for parties with interests in multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party submitting a short-form application that has an interest disclosed with respect to more than one short-form application must implement internal controls preventing any individual acting on behalf of the applicant from possessing information about the bids or bidding strategies of more than one party or communicating such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation of such internal controls does not preclude initiation of an investigation if warranted and will not outweigh specific evidence that a prohibited communication has occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to modify short-form for changes affecting licenses/agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must modify its short-form application to reflect any changes in ownership, membership of a consortium/joint venture, or agreements/understandings related to the licenses being auctioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that makes or receives a prohibited communication must report it in writing immediately, and in any case no later than five business days after the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be filed as directed in public notices detailing bidding procedures; if no public notice provides direction, report in writing to the Chief of the Auctions and Spectrum Access Division, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, by most expeditious means (including email). The obligation to report continues until the report has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for applicant and bids/bidding strategies for communications prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the communications prohibition: 'applicant' includes all controlling interests, holders of partnership and other ownership interests, any stock interest amounting to 10% or more, and all officers and directors of the entity submitting a short-form application; in a consortium each member is considered to have a controlling interest. 'Bids' or 'bidding strategies' include capital calls or requests for additional funds in support of bids or bidding strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example certification choices when ownership overlaps
rubrics_metrics.description: When ownership overlaps among applicants (example with Companies A-D), a party with interests in multiple applicants may avoid violating rules by certifying either that it has/will not communicate about bids or bidding strategies with certain parties, or that it has not/will not communicate with another specified party about bids or bidding strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete example of allowable certifications to preserve compliance when shared ownership exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special communications prohibition for broadcast television incentive auction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the broadcast television spectrum incentive auction, from the short-form filing deadline until results are announced, forward auction applicants are prohibited from communicating any incentive auction applicant's bids or bidding strategies to any full power or Class A broadcast television licensee, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception applies where a controlling interest, director, officer, or 10%+ owner in the forward auction applicant is also a controlling interest, director, officer, or governing board member of the broadcast licensee as of relevant deadlines. 'Controlling interests' defined as de jure/de facto control (see controlling interest definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upfront payment may be required and former-defaulter surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may require an upfront payment for licenses subject to competitive bidding; amount and procedures set in a Public Notice. An applicant that certifies it is a former defaulter must submit an upfront payment equal to 50% more than the otherwise required amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No interest will be paid on upfront payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upfront payment method requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upfront payments must be made by wire transfer in U.S. dollars from a financial institution whose deposits are insured by the FDIC and must be made payable to the Federal Communications Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to correct insufficient upfront payment before auction
rubrics_metrics.description: If an upfront payment is not compliant or insufficient, the applicant has a limited opportunity to correct the submission to meet the minimum valid upfront payment prior to the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not submit at least the minimum upfront payment, it will be ineligible to bid, its application will be dismissed, and any upfront payment made will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of upfront payments toward down payments and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder's upfront payment(s) will be credited toward any down payment required for licenses on which the bidder is the high bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where upfront exceeds required deposit of a winning bidder, the Commission may refund excess after determining no bid withdrawal penalties are owed. Upfront payments or down payments on deposit will be used to satisfy bid withdrawal or default penalties pursuant to § 1.2104 before being applied toward additional payment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Down payment timing and amount for high bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified by public notice, within ten business days after being notified that it is a high bidder, a high bidder must electronically submit such additional funds (down payment) as are necessary to bring its total deposits up to 20% of its high bid(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Down payments generally must be by wire transfer in U.S. dollars from an FDIC-insured financial institution payable to the FCC. Down payments will be held until award or returned (less applicable payments) if bidder unqualified or defaults. No interest on down payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form application filing requirement and consequences of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: A high bidder that meets its down payment obligations must, within ten business days after notification that it is a high bidder, submit a long-form application pursuant to service-specific rules; beginning Jan 1, 1999 all long-form applications must be filed electronically and applicants must submit required forms (e.g., FCC Form 602).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as otherwise provided in § 1.1104, no additional filing fee is required. Failure to submit required long-form application without good cause will be deemed default and subject to payments set forth in § 1.2104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form exhibit: disclosure of bidding consortia/agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: As an exhibit to its long-form application, the applicant must provide a detailed explanation of the terms, conditions, and parties involved in any bidding consortia, joint venture, partnership or other agreement or arrangement it entered into relating to the competitive bidding process prior to the time bidding was completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such agreements must have been entered into prior to filing short-form applications pursuant to § 1.2105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium post-winning-bid application and FRN rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A consortium that is a winning bidder may not apply as a consortium for licenses covered by the winning bids; individual members or new legal entities comprising members may apply for those licenses and shall use the consortium's FRN on their long-form applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within ten business days after public notice announcing grant of a long-form application, the licensee must update ULS to substitute its individual FRN for that of the consortium. An application by an individual member/new legal entity shall not constitute a major modification or change in control for related requirements and filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing eligibility for size-based benefits of newly formed entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuing eligibility for size-based benefits of a newly formed legal entity comprising two or more consortium members will be based on the size of that newly formed entity as of the filing of its long-form application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated-entity size attribution (gross revenues/assets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross revenues of the applicant (or licensee), its affiliates, its controlling interests, and affiliates of its controlling interests shall be attributed to the applicant and aggregated for purposes of determining eligibility for small business, very small business, or entrepreneur status, on a service-specific basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking status must disclose gross revenues for the previous five years (or two years for entrepreneur/where specified) separately and in the aggregate on short- and long-form applications. For certain services, total assets may be attributed per service-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of affiliate interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons or entities that hold interests in an applicant that are affiliates of each other or have an identity of interests will be treated as one person or entity and their ownership interests aggregated when determining compliance with size requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) If A & B together can control ABC Corp and both invest in DE Corp., their separate interests in DE Corp. must be aggregated. (2) Parent-subsidiary investments must be aggregated where affiliate relationship exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard to qualify for small business benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for small business benefits an applicant must (i) meet the applicable small business size standard and (ii) retain de jure and de facto control over the spectrum associated with the license(s) for which it seeks benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may lose eligibility for size-based benefits for one or more licenses without losing general eligibility so long as it retains de jure and de facto control of its overall business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium exception to aggregation for size-based benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant is a consortium of entities eligible for size-based bidding credits and/or closed bidding, the gross revenues and/or total assets of each consortium member shall not be aggregated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each consortium member must be a separate and distinct legal entity to qualify. Consortia that are winning bidders using this exception must comply with § 1.2107(g) as a condition of license grant. For rural-service-provider bidding credits, subscribers of consortium members are not aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants without identifiable controlling interests — attribution rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant cannot identify controlling interests under the standards in this section, the gross revenues of all interest holders in the applicant, and their affiliates, will be attributable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural telephone cooperative exception and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant (or controlling interest) may be exempt from certain attribution rules if organized as a cooperative under state law, is a 'rural telephone company' as defined by the Communications Act, and demonstrates eligibility for tax-exempt status or adherence to cooperative principles (Puget Sound Plywood factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no organic statute exists in the jurisdiction, the applicant must show valid organization and that articles/by-laws/organic documents provide operation pursuant to cooperative principles. If applicant is not an eligible rural telephone cooperative and has a controlling interest other than officers/directors, paragraph (a) applies with respect to officers/directors and such controlling interest only when that interest is an eligible rural telephone cooperative or controlled by one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-specific definition of small business
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will establish the definition of a small business on a service-specific basis, considering characteristics and capital requirements of the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restatement of controlling interest definition for designated-entity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of designated-entity rules, controlling interest includes individuals or entities with either de jure (evidenced by holdings >50% of voting stock or general partnership interests) or de facto control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De facto control is determined case-by-case with similar illustrative examples as elsewhere in the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and default deadlines and penalties for winning bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: Auction winners are required to pay the balance of winning bids in a lump sum within ten business days after a public notice establishes the payment deadline; a late payment within ten business days after the deadline is allowed with a late fee equal to 5% of the amount due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay by the late payment deadline is default and triggers applicable default payments and loss of license award. Withdrawal after bidding closed or failure to remit down payment within ten business days constitutes default and liability for default payments under § 1.2104. Commission may re-auction or offer licenses to other highest bidders (combinatorial auctions only re-auction). Violations of antitrust laws or Commission rules may lead to forfeiture of upfront/down/full bid and prohibition from future auctions.
